full_judgment:
Mr. Latifur Rahman, C. J:- This criminal petition for leave to appeal by the accused-petitioner is against the judgment and order dated 8.12.99 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division discharging the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 722 of 1994 for quashing the proceedings of Special Tribunal Case No_ 706 of 1992 of the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, 2nd Court and Special Tribunal No. 3, Dhaka arising out of Cantonment Police Station Case No. 28 dated 14.4,92 under Section 25B of the Special Powers Act, 1974. 

 19.10.93 the petitioner was implicated. Thereafter, the Special Tribunal took cognizance of the case and charge was framed against the petitioner on 3.5.94 for aiding the commission of the alleged offence. 

 for the accused-petitioner submits that thepresent petitioner has been implicated in this case on the basis of the confession of a co-accused and as such the learned Judges of the High Court Division acted illegally and wrongly in not quashing the proceedings. 

 statement of the co-accused cannot be considered at this stage because whatever probative value the confessional statement has got is a matter to be decided at the trial. So this argument of the learned Advocate for the petitioner cannot be entertained now for the purpose of quashing the proceeding. The learned Advocate cited the case of Lutfun Nahar Vs. State, 27 D. L. R. (AD) 29 

 and submitted that a confession of a co-accused is obviously a very weak type of evidence and as such the proceeding ought to have been quashed. It may be stated that the cited decision was a case wherein quashment was sought for against commitment of the accused for trial. In that reported decision it was found that there was no evidence upon which the order of commitment of the accused could be passed. But in our case the question of taking evidence has not yet arrived. At this stage we find prima facie allegations and materials for framing of the charge. In that view of the matter, this argument of the learned Advocate cannot be accepted. Mr. Malek
